verdict.rationale: Proa ships a first-party site layer that is Axum-backed and scaffolded with `proa new site`. It provides a generator-maintained route registry and a `proa site routes` route table. Renders get typed access to route state and loader caching through WebContext, and Suspense lets slow data stream without blocking the page. All of this is vendor-claimed only, and data fetching is mentioned in a single line, with no documented loader API or data-loading conventions. missing for 10: detailed data-fetching/loader documentation, a clear separately packaged meta-framework layer, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use an official full-stack meta-framework built on top of the framework for routing and data fetching

citations.quote: A minimal Axum-backed application with the core boundaries in place: proa new site hello-proa --yes
Register it in `src/routes.rs`, between the markers the generator maintains
Check the route table: proa site routes
Every render has typed access to request-scoped data, response metadata, route state, and loader caching through the same WebContext
let Suspense boundaries stream ready chunks out of order when slow data should not block the page
